name: RLPD
summary: RLPD showed that elaborate offline-to-online pipelines are largely unnecessary. Train off-policy from scratch, sample 50% of each minibatch from the prior dataset and 50% from fresh online interaction, add layer normalization and ensembling for stability, and you get faster and better results than pretrain-then-finetune schemes. Its simplicity made it the practical default for real-robot RL.
innovation: Symmetric sampling between offline and online buffers as a complete substitute for offline pretraining.
Identified layer normalization as the key stabilizer against value divergence.
matters: The efficiency backbone under SERL and much subsequent real-world manipulation RL.
limits: Assumes prior data is at least somewhat relevant to the target task.
lineage: A pragmatic simplification of offline-to-online RL built on SAC-style off-policy learning.
